thread:
Ashley M.: Heads up — seeing a spike of TLS handshake failures from eu-proxy around 08:12 UTC. ClientHello samples show missing SNI on a subset of requests. cc @Kevin R. @Ben C.
Ben C.: Yup, noticed that too. Correlating with a config roll from last night? quick grep shows many clienthello.server_name == '' in the last 30m.
Kevin R.: I also see a few KMS unwrap denies for the proxy service principal in the same window. logs: `ERROR keystore: unwrap failed, KMS_DECRYPT_DENIED principal=svc-proxy@redwood`
Ashley M.: rough count: ~60% missing SNI, and of those ~20% also have KMS unwrap deny. If SNI is gone, proxy chooses default cert and downstream mTLS fails and triggers keystore access that shouldn't be necessary. Possible path: LB forwarder stripping SNI then hitting internal proxy which tries to pick cert => keystore/KMS call => deny.
security-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 3770012345: tls_handshake_failure spike detected (eu). Details: https://internal/alerts/3770012345 — auto-sampled clienthello payloads attached.
Ben C.: Quick diagnostic command I ran: `jq -r '.client_hello.server_name' logs/*.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` -> shows lots of empty.
Lisa S.: Did we change the internal forwarder (fastfwd) last night? I saw a PR titled "preserve-sni=false by default" merged to fastfwd-config — @Ben was that you?
Ben C.: That was me — we flipped `preserve_sni: false` to try to avoid leaking upstream hostnames for a special tenant. I didn’t expect the chain to rely on SNI downstream. My bad.
Kevin R.: Ok that explains the missing SNI. Why are we seeing KMS denies though? The proxy should have a cached KEK and not call KMS for every handshake. Logs show `keystore.lookup` then `kms.unwrap` for default cert path. Maybe the proxy falls back to a different keystore key id when server_name is blank.
Ashley M.: hypothesis: fallback key id maps to a KMS key in eu region that the proxy principal doesn't have decrypt permission for after the recent RBAC scoping change. We tightened `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on svc-proxy last week.
Lisa S.: from security side: don't rotate keys or revoke roles yet. Priority: restore SNI preservation or add explicit route to select the correct cert without KMS calls. Plan: 1) revert fastfwd preserve_sni change (hotfix) 2) enable verbose proxy audit fields (proxy.sni, kms.principal, keystore.key_id) 3) run scoped decryption tests 4) follow-up RBAC review.
Ben C.: Rolling revert now to canary eu-forwarder-1. Command: `kubectl -n platform set env deployment/fastfwd-preserve --env=preserve_sni=true --record` — pushed to canary.
security-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for fastfwd-preserve (eu-forwarder-1). Link: https://ci/deploy/8812
Kevin R.: While canary spins up, a short mitigation: add a proxy config rule that maps empty SNI to the intended backends using `x-forwarded-host` if present. I'll prepare the change: snippet: ```
# envoy virtual host rule
match: {server_name: ''}
route: {cluster: "svc-default-host", set_host_header: "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-HOST)%"}
```
Ashley M.: Good. Also turn on KMS audit log tailing: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt"' --freshness=1h` and pipe to our aggregator. We need to capture which principals are being denied.
Ben C.: Canary looks healthy after 3 mins, handshake failure rate dropped ~85% in eu-canary. Rolling to eu-1 and eu-2 now.
Lisa S.: I've increased audit retention for proxy.sni and kms.principal for the incident window. Also opened ticket SEC-2026-219 for RBAC postmortem.
Kevin R.: Post-incident actions I propose: 1) test forwarder SNI changes in integration tests, 2) add a `reject_when_missing_sni` flag to surface potential mishandles, 3) tighten KMS role changes in a canary RBAC rollout.
Ashley M.: One more note: briefly saw a suspicious client IP that had missing SNI but valid cert relation — not evident MITM but we'll rotate if we see repeated anomalous principals. For now we're monitoring.
security-bot: incident SEC-2026-219 created and assigned to eng-security oncall.
Ashley M.: thanks all — will keep thread updated. Closing after 2h of stable metrics and clean KMS audit.
